fix: resolve MCP command PATH on Windows before spawning

On Windows, when MicroClaw is launched via `start /min` or as a
background service, the process inherits a stripped-down PATH that
may not include directories like `C:\Program Files\nodejs\`.

This causes MCP servers configured with bare commands like `"npx"`
to fail with "program not found" even though npx is installed.

Added `resolve_command()` that:
1. Returns absolute paths as-is
2. Tries `where` (Windows) / `which` (Unix) to resolve from PATH
3. Falls back to checking common install locations on Windows

Also fixed duplicate struct fields in config.rs from a merge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: add Playwright MCP extension mode setup guide

Chrome 136+ blocks --remote-debugging-port on the default user data
directory and DPAPI cookie encryption is path-bound on Windows, making
CDP-based browser sharing impossible without losing logins. Document
the Playwright MCP Bridge extension as the recommended solution — it
uses chrome.debugger API internally, bypassing both restrictions.

* feat: 4-layer memory stack for structured context injection

Replaces flat memory injection with a layered architecture inspired
by mempalace's progressive memory loading:

- L0 (Identity): PROFILE memories always loaded first, up to 20% of
  token budget. Sorted by confidence. Ensures agent always "knows"
  who the user is.

- L1 (Essential Story): Highest-confidence memories across all
  categories, up to next 30% of budget. These are durable facts the
  agent should always have available.

- L2 (Relevance): Query-matched memories via semantic (KNN) or
  keyword ranking, filling remaining budget. These are contextually
  relevant to what the user is currently asking.

- L3 (Deep Search): Not injected into system prompt. Available via

  retrieval when the agent needs more context.

Tracks the last N (tool_name, args_hash) keys across iterations. When the
same call would run for the (limit+1)th time inside the window, the agent

change approach instead of repeating itself. Defaults to a 10-call window
with a limit of 3; both knobs are configurable.

  - the agent ran tool calls but emitted no closing text
  - more than half of tool_results errored

the agent loop enqueues chat_id to AppState.skill_review_queue right

the queue (deduping bursts) and runs the review pipeline.

  - reviews fire seconds after a turn ends, not up to reflector_interval_mins
    later, so context is fresh and feedback loops are tight
  - each conversation is reviewed once per completion, not once per
    reflector tick (no more re-reviewing the same chat on every tick)

* feat: port hermes-agent prompt cache, fuzzy edit, guardrails, checkpoints, @-refs, subdir hints

Bundle of six focused ports from nousresearch/hermes-agent, all
opt-in or non-disruptive by default, fully unit-tested.

1. Anthropic prompt-cache breakpoints (`src/prompt_cache.rs`).
   Inserts up to 4 `cache_control` markers per Anthropic request —
   system prompt + last 3 messages — so multi-turn chats hit the
   prompt cache (~75% input cost reduction). On by default for
   Anthropic; OpenAI-compat path untouched. New config:
   `anthropic_prompt_cache_enabled` (default true),
   `anthropic_prompt_cache_ttl` ("5m" or "1h"). Implementation
   mutates the serialized JSON body just before send, so the typed
   `MessagesRequest`/`Message`/`ContentBlock` shapes stay clean.
   Hermes ref: `agent/prompt_caching.py`.

2. Fuzzy `edit_file` matching (`src/tools/fuzzy_match.rs`).
   When `old_string` doesn't byte-match exactly, retries an 8-strategy
   chain: line-trimmed, whitespace-normalized, indentation-flexible,
   escape-normalized (`\n` -> newline), trimmed-boundary,
   unicode-normalized (smart quotes, em/en-dash, NBSP), block-anchor
   (first/last line + middle similarity). Returns which strategy
   succeeded. Includes the escape-drift guard from upstream so a
   tool-call that smuggled in `\'`/`\"` artifacts is rejected before
   it corrupts the file. Hermes ref: `tools/fuzzy_match.py`
   (originally from OpenCode).

3. Per-turn tool-loop guardrails (`src/tool_guardrails.rs`).
   Sits alongside the existing duplicate-call circuit breaker and
   adds two finer-grained signals: (a) idempotent no-progress —
   when a read-only tool returns the same result hash N times for
   the same args, append a guidance suffix asking the model to use
   what it already has; (b) same-tool failure streak — when ANY tool
   fails N times this turn (across different args), append guidance
   to change approach. Pure observation: results still go to the
   model with extra hints, never blocked. New `IDEMPOTENT_TOOLS`
   constant in `src/tools/mod.rs` classifies the 13 read-only tools.
   Hermes ref: `agent/tool_guardrails.py`.

4. Filesystem checkpoints via shadow git (`src/checkpoint.rs`).
   Once-per-turn `git add -A && git commit` against a shadow repo
   under `<data_dir>/checkpoints/<sha256(abs_path)[:16]>/` whose
   `GIT_DIR` lives outside the user's working tree. New `/rewind`
   chat command lists the most recent 20 snapshots; `/rewind <hash>`
   restores. Off by default — opt in via `checkpoints_enabled: true`.
   Shadow repo isolates from `~/.gitconfig` (no signing prompts, no
   hooks, no credential helpers). Commit-hash validation rejects
   leading `-` and non-hex strings to defeat git argument injection.
   Hermes ref: `tools/checkpoint_manager.py`.

5. `@`-prefix context references (`src/context_references.rs`).
   `@file:src/main.rs`, `@folder:src/`, `@diff`, `@staged`,
   `@url:https://example.com` in user messages expand server-side
   into an attached-context block before the LLM sees the message.
   File refs support `:N` and `:start-end` line ranges. URL fetches
   delegate to `microclaw_tools::web_fetch::fetch_url_with_timeout`
   so the SSRF guard from PR #335 still applies. Sensitive-path
   block list refuses `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`,
   `~/.docker`, `~/.azure` and `~/.bashrc`/`.netrc`/`.npmrc`/etc.
   No new config — the runtime resolves the chat's working dir as
   the expansion root. Hermes ref: `agent/context_references.py`.

6. Subdirectory `AGENTS.md` hints (`src/subdirectory_hints.rs`).
   Lazy progressive context loading: when a tool call touches
   `backend/main.py`, microclaw walks up to 5 ancestor directories
   looking for `AGENTS.md` / `agents.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `claude.md`
   / `.cursorrules`, and appends the first hit (capped at 8K chars)
   to that tool's result. The chat root is excluded — its hint is
   already loaded into the system prompt. Each directory is emitted
   at most once per turn. Hermes ref: `agent/subdirectory_hints.py`.

Wiring lives in `src/agent_engine.rs:process_with_agent_logic`:
@-refs run on the latest user message before system-prompt build,
the per-turn checkpoint snapshot runs once before the agent loop,
and the guardrail/subdir-hint controllers run inside the post-tool
walk that already enforces the duplicate-call breaker. The
`chat_working_dir` helper in `microclaw-tools/runtime.rs` is now
public so the agent loop and `/rewind` can resolve the same chat
working directory the tools see.

sensitive-path blocking, and subdir-hint ancestor walking. Full

Three orthogonal lifecycle controls for scheduled tasks, composable
with each other and with completion contracts:

- schedule_type "random": next firing lands uniformly at random inside
  a duration window ("2h..3d", units s/m/h/d/w/mo) after each run;
  windows clamped to [1 min, 366 days]; UUID-CSPRNG entropy, injected
  in tests.
- max_runs: retire as completed after N runs.
- not_after: retire once the next firing would pass the deadline,
  re-checked at claim time.

primitive (concrete next_run, or completed with a logged reason);

fix(engine): render stable timestamps on user messages

Re-rendering an unchanged session history must produce byte-identical
text, otherwise the prompt-cache prefix misses on every turn (#490).

Stored `messages.timestamp` values carried sub-second precision, so
format_user_message now truncates them to whole seconds in UTC and
emits them as an RFC 3339 `ts` attribute on `<user_message>`. Messages
without a parseable timestamp keep the previous format unchanged.

fix(plugins): sort manifests so tool order is stable

`load_plugin_report` iterated `read_dir`, whose order is arbitrary on most
filesystems. That order flowed into `dynamic_plugin_tool_definitions` and
therefore into the tool definitions the provider caches, so the cached
prefix reshuffled between restarts. Sort manifests by name.

feat(llm): report prompt-cache token usage

Prompt caching is only useful if you can see it working, and there was no
way to tell a cache miss from a provider that never reports cache counts.

Usage now carries cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens.
Parsers read them from the three shapes providers use: Anthropic-style
top-level fields, OpenAI chat `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, and
Responses `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. All are optional and
default to zero. Agent metrics aggregate them and export them as
`gen_ai.usage.cache_*` span attributes.

feat(config): add system_prompt_time_detail

The system prompt used to embed `current_local_time` and `current_utc_time`
on every build, so the cached prompt prefix changed each turn and prompt
caching never hit.

This adds an enum controlling how much clock detail the system prompt
carries, defaulting to `date` (stable for a whole local day). `full`
restores the previous behavior; `none` drops the time lines entirely. The
live clock still reaches the model through the `get_current_time` tool and
the per-turn context block.

refactor(engine): split query-scoped skills and memory from stable layers

Both catalogs were rendered against the current user query and then
inlined into the system prompt, so the cached prefix shifted with every
question. Split each into a stable half and a query-scoped half:

- memory: `split_db_memory_context` separates Identity/Essential (stable
  per chat) from Relevant/Connected (query-ranked)
- skills: `build_skills_catalog` is the canonical query-independent
  listing; new `build_skills_hot_bodies_for_query` renders just the
  inlined bodies for skills matching the query

Scoring logic is unchanged — it moved into a shared `rank_skills_for_query`
so `build_skills_catalog_for_query` keeps its exact prior behavior.

fix(engine): move per-turn context out of the cached system prompt

The system prompt is the provider's cache prefix, and it was carrying
data that changes every turn: the live clock, query-matched memories,
inlined skill bodies, the mood read, verified prior experiences, plugin
context, and the relationship hint. The prefix therefore never matched a
previous request and every turn paid full input cost.

Introduce a `<turn_context>` block carrying exactly that data, delivered
as its own system message immediately after the system prompt. The
cached prefix in front of it is now byte-stable across turns.

The system prompt keeps what genuinely belongs there: identity and
static rules, the canonical skills catalog, stable memory layers, and
identity/project/user-model context.

test: assert ts attribute and document prompt-cache behavior

Update the Telegram history assertions for the `ts` attribute, and
document `system_prompt_time_detail` in the example config, site

test: cover prompt-prefix stability invariants

Locks in the #490 guarantees that were previously only implicit:

- system prompt is byte-identical across turns with the clock disabled,
  and varies only in the date line under date mode
- date mode emits a well-formed YYYY-MM-DD in the configured timezone
- memory split partitions by section, asserted against real builder
  output rather than hand-written strings
- build_skills_hot_bodies_for_query covers match/no-match/top_k=0/blank
  and excludes the cold listing
- canonical skills catalog is deterministic and name-ordered
- plugin manifests are name-ordered, independent of read_dir order
- system_prompt_time_detail parses each variant, defaults to date when
  absent, and rejects unknown values instead of silently degrading

fix(engine): attach turn context at request time instead of persisting it

The `<turn_context>` block was inserted into `messages` as a `system`-role
entry and then written to the session with the rest of the history, so it
accumulated one copy per turn (three turns -> three stale clocks sent to the
provider) and put a `system` role into the messages array, which the
Anthropic Messages API rejects. Sitting at `messages[0]` it also invalidated
the cached prefix right after the system prompt, so the conversation history
was still re-prefilled every turn.

Build the block as before, but keep it out of `messages`: `attach_turn_context`
clones the history at each provider call and prepends the block to the latest
plain user message (the same anchor `safe_compact_split` uses). The persisted
history and everything ahead of that message stay byte-identical, tool-loop
iterations only append after it, and no `system` role reaches the provider.
The block is now always emitted so the live clock is never dropped, and the
system prompt documents the `ts` attribute and the `<turn_context>` block.

Adds a three-turn regression test with a recording provider plus a unit test
for the anchor selection, and updates the CHANGELOG / docs wording.
